question.leadin: Answer the following about a defunct Cabinet position.
question.text: This member of Franklin Pierce's cabinet later became the first and only president of the Confederate States of America.
question.clue: Franklin Pierce made this man his Secretary of War, after which this politician won election to the U.S. Senate from Mississippi for a second time.

swap.leadin: The repulsion of Pickett's Charge at Cemetery Ridge secured victory in this battle for Union forces.
swap.text: Identify this pivotal battle of the Civil War in Pennsylvania, where Joshua Chamberlain led Union forces in a downhill bayonet charge at Little Round Top.
swap.clue: During this battle, Lewis Armistead valiantly led his brigade to the "high water mark of the Confederacy" when he broke through enemy lines near the "bloody angle".

question.text: This futile charge, led by James Longstreet and its namesake, was disastrous for the Confederacy. The Union's Winfield Scott Hancock commanded against it.
question.clue: The brigades of General James Kemper were fired upon at this event by a division of Abner Doubleday's men on Cemetery Ridge.

swap.leadin: Name these candidates in the Election of 1860.
swap.text: This man was famous for introducing the idea of "popular sovereignty" and was largely responsible for the Compromise of 1850. He engaged in a series of debates with the eventual winner of this election.
swap.clue: This "Little Giant" from Illinois who defended popular sovereignty in his Freeport Doctrine.

question.leadin: After experiencing the Great Disappointment in 1843, this woman distanced herself from her Millerite friends.
question.text: Name this woman who became an abolitionist after an intense religious experience, saying "The Spirit calls me, and I must go."
question.clue: One speech by this thinker repeats the question "Where did your Christ come from?" and mentions "this thing in the head" called "intellect."

swap.text: This proposal was not a compromise, but it did try to prohibit slavery in the Mexican cession. It was fervently supported by Republicans.
swap.clue: This piece of legislation was drafted with the help of Preston King, Jacob Brinkerhoff, and Gideon Welles.

question.leadin: Answer the following about major Confederate victories during the Civil War.
question.text: General Ambrose Burnside tried to cross the Rappahannock River during this battle in order to get closer to the Confederate capital of Richmond. It is often cited as the most lopsided Confederate victory of the war.
question.clue: Though it isn't Antietam, during the first battle at this location, Prospect Hill and the Sunken Road were key defensive points.

swap.text: Thaddeus Stevens and this Massachusetts senator were two of the most influential Radical Republicans. This politician attacked Senator Andrew Butler in the "Crime Against Kansas" speech.
swap.clue: This man had earlier described Stephen Douglass as the "Sancho Panza" to a man derided for his "incoherent phrases" and hoped that "South Carolina" would " howling."

question.leadin: Name these other people involved in the 1824 election.
question.text: Both Adams and Andrew Jackson supported this man for the Vice-Presidency; he thus received the office.
question.clue: On his deathbed, Andrew Jackson regretted that he had not executed this man, his former Vice President, for treason.

swap.text: The song states that "[this general] bold and gay, set forth the shortest way, by Manassas." That campaign's failure came with this general's defeat at the First Battle of Bull Run.
swap.clue: McClellan had earlier taken over the Army of the Potomac after this man fared poorly at the First Battle of Bull Run. He was also blamed for the Union's failures at the Second Battle of Bull Run.

question.text: This meticulous organizer and perpetual delayer was the Union commander at the Seven Days. This man served as head of the Army of the Potomac, and was the Democratic opponent of Lincoln in the 1864 election.
question.clue: His most important tactical victory came after his army absorbed John Pope's forces and was keyed by a discovery of the lost Special Order 191.

swap.leadin: The Marais du Cygne massacre took place during this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict between pro-slavery Border Ruffians and anti-slavery Free-Staters in a namesake US territory from 1854 to 1861.
swap.clue: The Free State Hotel was targeted by a side in this conflict.

question.leadin: Note to players: two answers required. A law named for these two states broke a convention that declared slavery was banned north of the 36°30' ("thirty-six thirty") parallel.
question.text: Identify these two states that name an 1854 act that advocated for "popular sovereignty". The act led to one of these states's "Bleeding" period, which saw conflict between "jayhawkers" and "border ruffians".
question.answerHtml: Kansas and Nebraska [accept Kansas-Nebraska Act, prompt on partial answers, prompt on Bleeding Kansas]

swap.leadin: This woman mocked her former suitor Stephen Douglas by calling him "a very little, little giant, by the side of my tall Kentuckian... intellectually my husband towers above Douglas just as he does physically."
swap.text: Name this woman, who rejected Douglas in part due to her Whig politics. This woman's chronic migraines and depression worsened after the premature deaths of her sons, Willie and Tad.
swap.clue: This woman caused a scandal by wearing lilac instead of black at a funeral and asked "I wonder if the women of Washington expect me to muffle myself in mourning for every soldier killed?"

question.text: Some Copperheads also belonged to this secret society that wanted to annex slavery-friendly territory surrounding the Caribbean. They sold fake coupons promising protection from Confederate raiders to Pennsylvania farmers.
question.clue: This organization's last leader was Clement Vallandigham when it was known as the Order of the Sons of Liberty, prior to which it was called the Order of American Knights.

swap.leadin: Clarina Nichols lobbied to ensure a guarantee for property rights and limited voting for women in this document.
swap.text: Name this 1859 constitution, under which Kansas joined the U.S. as a free state.

question.leadin: Name some people in the Confederate cabinet of Jefferson Davis.
question.text: Before becoming Davis' Secretary of War, this Jewish fellow was Attorney General for him. After being blamed for some humiliating defeats, he resigned and was appointed Secretary of State by Davis in 1862. He escaped to England after the war where he was a quite successful lawyer.
question.clue: This politician who was the first self-professed Jew to be elected to the Senate. After the Civil War, he fled to England, became a barrister, and wrote the influential Treatise on the Law of Sale of Personal Property.

swap.leadin: Name these urban political bosses of the 19th century.
swap.text: This man served as Mayor of New York City twice. During his first term, this man was arrested by the state-appointed Metropolitan police department, and during his second, he suggested that New York secede from the US.
swap.clue: This opponent of George Walling twice served as mayor of New York City during the mid -1800s. He proposed that the city join the Confederacy to maintain cotton profits and served two terms in the House of Representatives in the 1860s, during which Henry Dawes proposed a measure to censor him for his use of inappropriate language.

question.leadin: Name some things about failed Constitutional amendments.
question.text: This 1861 amendment was introduce in the Senate by William H. Seward. It would have prohibited even a Constitutional amendment from abolishing or interfering with any state or its "domestic institutions thereof."
question.clue: This amendment, an attempt to deal with the slavery question, would have amended the Constitution to prevent further amendments pertaining to slavery.

swap.leadin: Name these heroes of nutty post-Reconstruction southern politics.
swap.text: This Senator opposed the Funding Act of 1870 in Virginia as leader of the Readjuster party, which sought a reduction in state debt. This dude, known as "Little Billy," gained fame as the hero of the "Battle of the Crater" during the siege of Petersburg.
